chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa — all together from Ibn Mahbub, from Abu Usama, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Ishaq al-Sabi'i, from the one who narrated to him among those who are trusted — he said:

I heard the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) saying: 'Verily, the people, after the Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family), divided into three [groups]. They divided to: a scholar upon guidance from God, whom God had made self-sufficient with what he knew, from the knowledge of others; and an ignorant one claiming to have knowledge — with no knowledge for him — being self-conceited by what he possesses, while the world had tempted him, and he tempted others; and a student learning from a scholar upon the way of guidance from God and salvation. Then, those who claimed (falsely) perished, and those who fabricated (lies) were lost.'

key_terms.آلُوا: Divided/turned/ended up — denotes a movement toward or adoption of a position
key_terms.جَاهِلٌ مُدَّعٍ: Ignorant claimant — one who falsely claims knowledge without possessing it
key_terms.عَالِمٌ: Scholar — one with genuine divinely-guided knowledge
key_terms.مُتَعَلِّمٌ: Seeker of knowledge/student — one actively learning from a true scholar
key_terms.هُدًى مِنَ اللَّهِ: Guidance from God — knowledge that is divinely sourced, not merely intellectual

ai.seo_question: What are the three types of people Imam Ali described after the Prophet?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) describes the three types of people following the Prophet's era: the true scholar whose divine knowledge makes him independent of others' flawed learning, the dangerous pretender who deceives himself and misleads others, and the sincere student who follows authentic guidance. This teaching was likely delivered in the aftermath of the early Islamic schism when false authorities were emerging, warning the community to distinguish genuine scholarship from fraudulent claims. The term 'هُدًى مِنَ اللَّهِ' (guidance from God) specifically denotes divinely-sourced knowledge, implying the Imam himself as the authentic channel of such guidance.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Muhammad, from Sahl Bin Ziyad and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Asama, from Hisham Bin Salim, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Is’haq Al Sabi’e, from the one who narrated it, from the one is relied with it, said,

‘I heard Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The people split after Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> into three – a group went to a scholar<sup>asws</sup> who was upon Guidance from Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, whom Allah<sup>azwj</sup> had Made to be self-sufficient with what he<sup>asws</sup> knew, from the knowledge of others; and (a group went to) an ignorant one claiming to (have the) knowledge, (although) there was no knowledge for him, being astounded (confused) by whatever was with him. The world had tempted him and he tempted others; and (a group went to) a student of the scholar<sup>asws</sup> upon the way of Guidance from Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and were saved. Then they were destroyed, the ones who claimed (to be scholars), and the ones who forged (matters) incurred loss’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Muhammad from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa all from ibn Mahbub from abu ’Usama from Hisham ibn Salim from abu Hamza from abu Ishaq al-Sabay‘i from one who narrated it from a reliable source from Imam Ali (a.s.) who has said the following.

“After the holy Prophet people become of three kinds. One group went to a divinely well guided scholar. Allah had given him such a high degree of knowledge that made him independent of the knowledge of the others. The second group was the ignorant group, who claimed to have knowledge but in fact they had no knowledge. This was an egotist group. The worldly attractions had made them to lose sight of the truth and to mislead other people. The third group consisted of those people who learned from a divinely guided scholar who taught them for the sake of Allah and for their salvation. It then was obvious that those who claimed (to be scholars while, in fact, they were not scholars) and those who forged certain matters falsely were destroyed.”
